claims.text: The target material is a rare-earth-free high-entropy alloy composed of transition metals such as Fe, Co, Ni, and Mn.
Optimizing alloy composition can produce near-zero magnetic anisotropy.
Optimizing alloy composition can place the Curie temperature close to the operating temperature.
Near-zero magnetic anisotropy governs a strong magnetocaloric response at low applied fields.
A Curie temperature close to the operating temperature governs a strong magnetocaloric response at low applied fields.
Near-zero magnetic anisotropy and alignment of the Curie and operating temperatures enable rapid heat exchange.
Near-zero magnetic anisotropy and alignment of the Curie and operating temperatures produce low hysteresis.
Near-zero magnetic anisotropy and alignment of the Curie and operating temperatures maintain mechanical stability.
A composition optimized for magnetic anisotropy and Curie temperature will have a stronger low-field magnetocaloric response than an unoptimized composition.
The proposed hypothesis is intended to apply at applied magnetic fields below 2 T.
The proposed hypothesis is intended to apply at operating temperatures near the alloy's Curie temperature.
